home.headline: ML Engineer with Deep Roots in Manufacturing & Physical Systems
about: I build production ML systems with a foundation that most ML engineers don't have: real manufacturing experience. My background spans the full engineering lifecycle—mechanical design with GD&T, production cost estimation, validation testing, and quality systems—giving me first-principles intuition for the hardware and processes that ML models are ultimately deployed against.

On the ML side, I design and ship end-to-end systems: drift detection pipelines, registry-driven model promotion, containerized inference services on AWS, and structured test frameworks with fault injection and CI-enabled validation. I think carefully about leakage, reproducibility, and what it means for a model to be production-ready—not just accurate on a holdout set.

This combination lets me move fluently between the data and the physical world—understanding sensor behavior, failure modes, and manufacturing constraints at the level of depth that produces better features, better models, and systems that are actually trusted on the factory floor.
B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering from Waterloo (AI Option, Co-op) · Master of Data Science from UBC.

highlights: Graduate training in applied machine learning, MLOps, and data-driven decision making.
Strong emphasis on end-to-end ML systems, reproducibility, and production readiness.
Artificial Intelligence Option and Management Science Option.
Strong foundation in systems engineering, controls, and applied mathematics.

work.title: Systems Engineer
work.subtitle: Sensor data validation and monitoring for industrial equipment.
highlights: Built a sensor data validation pipeline processing multi-rate telemetry and waveform inputs to generate interpretable health scores across 12 machine metrics for production monitoring.
Implemented leakage-free expanding-window CV (5 splits, N=3,045) with structured OOF evaluation, achieving R²=0.39 vs. negative baseline to ensure test results reflect true deployment performance.
Deployed monitoring dashboards to track performance metrics, anomaly trends, and qualification auditability.

work.title: AWS Cloud Engineer / Cloud Architect
work.subtitle: Cloud infrastructure automation and operational efficiency.
highlights: Delivered a standardized EC2 "golden image" with preinstalled essential applications, streamlining server deployment and improving provisioning efficiency by approximately 80%.
Automated the generation of monthly dashboards to visualize AWS usage and costs, improving operational visibility and decision-making.
Worked closely with infrastructure and operations teams to standardize cloud environments and improve reliability across AWS deployments.

work.title: Data Scientist Research Assistant
work.subtitle: Computer vision research for satellite-based ice concentration analysis.

projects.title: Manufacturing Test Automation Platform
projects.tagline: Dockerized test framework with yield analytics and fault injection for manufacturing validation.
bullets: Developed a TCP/IP-based DUT simulator to emulate manufacturing test communication, control, and faults.
Designed structured acceptance and qualification test plans with defined coverage mapping, retry logic, and step-level validation criteria tied to product requirements.
Implemented an automated test framework supporting multi-SN execution, structured JSON logging, fault injection (timeouts, drift, intermittent failure), and traceable result storage.
Built yield analytics modules (FPY, FTY, Pareto, stratification) and deployed a Dockerized, CI-enabled validation pipeline with auto-generated qualification reports.
projects.summary: End-to-end manufacturing test automation platform featuring a TCP/IP-based DUT simulator, structured acceptance and qualification test plans, fault injection, and yield analytics. The system produces traceable structured logs and auto-generated qualification reports through a Dockerized, CI-enabled validation pipeline.

projects.title: Robotic Manipulator System
projects.tagline: Hardware-in-the-loop validation system for closed-loop robotic control and trajectory testing.
bullets: Integrated motors, sensors, and Arduino control for closed loop hardware validation testing.
Developed manual and automated control modes to validate trajectory accuracy and repeatability.
Performed system identification and parameter tuning to resolve instability and coupling effects.
Executed structured troubleshooting and root cause analysis to improve control robustness.
Validated performance under varying load and motion profiles to ensure stable operation.
projects.summary: Closed-loop robotic manipulator system integrating motors, sensors, and Arduino-based control for hardware validation. The project covers manual and automated control modes, system identification, parameter tuning, and structured root cause analysis to ensure trajectory accuracy and stable operation under varied conditions.

projects.title: Time-Series Forecasting with Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)
projects.tagline: Multi-horizon stock price forecasting with interpretable transformer models.
bullets: Applied a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to model and forecast Tesla stock prices using historical market data, producing probabilistic multi-horizon forecasts.
Engineered time-based and rolling statistical features, and structured inputs into static, known, and unknown variables to align with TFT’s architecture.
Evaluated model performance against a naive persistence baseline using expanding-window cross-validation, reporting RMSE, MAE, and R² across forecast horizons.
Analyzed model interpretability through variable importance and attention weights to understand which features and historical timesteps most influenced predictions.
projects.summary: Developed an interpretable time-series forecasting pipeline using Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to predict Tesla stock prices over multiple future horizons. The project emphasizes rigorous time-series validation, baseline comparison, and model interpretability, demonstrating a data-science–driven approach to transformer-based forecasting.

projects.title: ML Guard
projects.tagline: Lightweight ML monitoring and cost guard with explicit drift detection.
bullets: Built a lightweight ML monitoring service to track inference latency, prediction distributions, feature statistics, and data drift from a single event stream.
Implemented baseline-driven drift detection (PSI for numeric, frequency divergence for categorical) with timezone-aware daily aggregation.
Added Slack-based alerting for drift and operational regressions via a background worker architecture.
Integrated AWS Cost Explorer (best-effort) to enable per-project cost visibility without coupling core monitoring to cloud credentials.
projects.summary: ML Guard is a lightweight monitoring and observability system for ML inference pipelines. It computes latency metrics, prediction statistics, feature distributions, and baseline-driven drift signals from a single event stream, with optional AWS cost attribution and Slack alerting. The system prioritizes production correctness, low operational overhead, and clear monitoring signals over platform complexity.

projects.title: Production-Grade MLOps System for Stock Price Forecasting
projects.tagline: Registry-driven ML deployment with AutoML and transformer-based models on AWS.
bullets: Built a production-ready MLOps system enabling reliable training, promotion, and serving of time-series forecasting models across local and AWS environments.
Integrated multiple model families—including classical baselines, AutoML (FLAML), and transformer-based models from Hugging Face—under a single MLflow registry and serving interface.
Implemented registry-backed model promotion with explicit aliasing (‘@prod’) to decouple experimentation from production inference.
Deployed a containerized FastAPI inference service on AWS ECS behind an Application Load Balancer, validated through live end-to-end prediction requests.
projects.summary: Designed and deployed a production-grade MLOps system for time-series forecasting that supports multiple modeling approaches, including AutoML and transformer-based models from Hugging Face. The project emphasizes operational correctness through registry-driven model promotion, reproducible training, and live cloud inference on AWS, demonstrating end-to-end ownership from experimentation to production serving.

projects.title: Machine Health Prediction & Monitoring Dashboard
projects.tagline: Predictive maintenance system for industrial equipment using interpretable ML.
bullets: Developed an end-to-end predictive maintenance system using real-world industrial sensor data.
Built and evaluated multiple machine learning models (Ridge, Random Forest, LSTM), balancing accuracy with interpretability for operational use.
Performed feature engineering and time-series modeling to forecast equipment health and potential failures.
Designed and implemented an interactive Dash dashboard to visualize real-time health scores, historical trends, and maintenance alerts.
Structured the system with deployment-readiness, reproducibility, and monitoring in mind.
projects.summary: End-to-end predictive maintenance system built on real-world industrial sensor data, combining interpretable machine learning, time-series feature engineering, and deployment-ready workflows. The project delivers real-time equipment health scoring, failure forecasting, and operational visibility through an interactive Dash dashboard, with a strong emphasis on reproducibility and monitoring.

projects.title: AI Wall Painting Robot – Wall Segmentation
projects.tagline: Deep learning-based wall surface segmentation for robotic painting automation.
bullets: Implemented a Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSPNet) for industrial wall segmentation.
Designed an encoder–decoder architecture with a PPM-based decoder for pixel-wise classification.
Evaluated multiple training strategies including transfer learning and end-to-end training.
Achieved 92.13% accuracy and 72.58% IoU, enabling reliable automated wall-surface detection.
Preprocessed data by flattening irregular wall segments, resizing images, and applying data augmentation.
projects.summary: Deep learning–based wall surface segmentation system for robotic painting automation, using a PSPNet encoder–decoder architecture with pyramid pooling. The model achieves high accuracy and IoU through careful data preprocessing, augmentation, and training strategy evaluation, enabling reliable pixel-level wall detection in industrial environments.
